clinicalPearls: A lethal ciliopathy characterised by central nervous system malformation, polydactyly and midline facial defects
Hydrocephalus or absent midline brain structures with a characteristic keyhole-shaped defect of the occipital bone is typical
Polydactyly is usually postaxial in the hands and preaxial (with a duplicated great toe) in the feet
Micrognathia, cleft lip or palate and abnormal genitalia are frequent
Shows considerable overlap with Meckel-Gruber and acrocallosal syndromes, reflecting shared ciliary and hedgehog pathway biology
The Finnish form is caused by variants in HYLS1, while KIF7 variants produce an overlapping phenotype
The condition is almost always lethal before or shortly after birth
reference.pathophysiology: Hydrolethalus syndrome is caused by biallelic variants in HYLS1 or, in overlapping cases, KIF7, both of which encode proteins that function at the basal body and primary cilium. Because the primary cilium transduces hedgehog signalling that patterns the neural tube, midline face and limbs, loss of these proteins disrupts development of midline brain structures, producing hydrocephalus or their absence together with the distinctive occipital bone defect. The same disturbance of ciliary hedgehog signalling in the limb bud generates the postaxial and preaxial polydactyly, while impaired midline patterning underlies the facial clefting and micrognathia. The severe, multisystem malformation reflects the central role of the cilium in early embryonic signalling and accounts for the lethal outcome and overlap with other ciliopathies.
additionalInvestigations: Detailed antenatal ultrasound and, where appropriate, post-mortem examination
Brain imaging to define the midline malformation and hydrocephalus
Skeletal radiographs to characterise polydactyly and the occipital defect
Karyotype or chromosomal microarray to exclude a chromosomal cause such as trisomy 13
Molecular testing of HYLS1 and KIF7 within a ciliopathy gene panel
redFlags: Antenatal findings of hydrocephalus, polydactyly and a midline defect indicating a likely lethal ciliopathy
Severe respiratory and neurological compromise at birth
A high recurrence risk requiring genetic counselling before future pregnancies
reference.prognosis: The condition is almost uniformly lethal in the perinatal period; management is directed at diagnosis, compassionate care and genetic counselling, with a one-in-four recurrence risk in future pregnancies given autosomal recessive inheritance.
pitfalls: Mistaking the condition for isolated hydrocephalus and missing the syndromic diagnosis
Confusing it with Meckel-Gruber or acrocallosal syndrome without genetic testing
Failing to arrange genetic counselling for the high recurrence risk
Overlooking the characteristic keyhole-shaped occipital bone defect
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
